gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the makers' own US stores today (2026-11-13), the UGREEN DXP2800 at $389.99 is the only in-stock NAS under $400 that uses the 12th-gen-or-newer Intel N-series chip Jellyfin recommends. TerraMaster's store has the F2-425 Plus at $469.99, the F4-425 at $429.99 and the N95 F2-424 sold out at $379.99. Every TerraMaster that does fit the budget uses an older Intel chip of the kind Jellyfin's hardware guide says to avoid.
standout_why: I compared four rival pages. Starry Hope's best-2-bay page (2026-10-31, cited) lists the F2-425 Plus at $499.99 'now' and the DXP2800 at a $389.99 list price. It does not price the F4-425 or F2-424, and it does not say that no other qualifying chip fits under $400. ComputingForGeeks' QuickSync picks page (updated 2026-11-11) gives only price ranges ('about $370 to $390' for the DXP2800) and leaves out the F2-425 Plus, F4-425 and F2-424. ubnas (cited) gives no prices at all. Jellyfin's hardware-selection doc (cited) says to avoid older low-power Intel chips but has no prices. The ChatGPT answers showed the F2-425 Plus at $375.99 to $399.49 and the F4-425 at $386.99, which TerraMaster's own store no longer matches. They also called the F2-425 Plus a strong under-$400 alternative.
decides: This confirms the DXP2800 as the pick and removes the rival ChatGPT kept suggesting. At maker prices the F2-425 Plus is $70 over budget, so it can't be the under-$400 alternative. Every TerraMaster that does fit the budget (F2-425 at $269.99, and the F2-423 and F4-423 that ChatGPT showed) uses a chip type Jellyfin says to avoid. The ChatGPT cards priced the DXP2800 at $296.99 on Walmart, but Walmart blocked our check. If that listing is gone, the DXP2800 still fits at $389.99 from UGREEN.
